Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Jordan Brooks
Member ID: W436997835
Reference number: POC-41FE448BEA-64337
Date of denial notice: 2026-08-23
Service at issue: Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914
Appeal deadline: This appeal is submitted within the 180-day deadline stated in your notice (by 2027-02-19).

To the Appeals Department:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914) recommended by my treating surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, MD, Orthopedic Surgery. Your notice states the denial reason as: "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity." I am requesting that Regence reverse this determination because my clinical record satisfies the medical-necessity criteria set out in Regence's own governing policy for this procedure.

Governing policy identified

Based on my review, the applicable document is the Regence Medical Policy Manual, Surgery, Policy No. 160, "Femoroacetabular Impingement Surgery" (Effective: March 1, 2026; Last Review: January 2026), available at https://blue.regence.com/trgmedpol/surgery/sur160.pdf. I understand this policy states it was scheduled for revision effective October 1, 2026. Because my prior authorization request was reviewed before that date, I ask Regence to confirm in writing which version of Policy No. 160 (and which specific criteria) was applied to my request, and to apply that version — or, if the revised version was actually applied, to identify that version and its criteria so I can respond to the correct standard.

That policy states, in the version I was able to retrieve:

"I. Open or arthroscopic surgical treatment of femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) may be medically necessary in skeletally mature patients when all of the following criteria (A-E) are met:"

I address each criterion below using the documentation already in my prior authorization packet.

Criterion A — "Moderate-to-severe hip pain that is worsened by flexion activities (e.g., squatting or prolonged sitting) that significantly limits activities"

My record documents 9 months of progressive hip pain, unrelieved by rest, with sharp anterior groin pain triggered specifically by sitting and pivoting. I am currently unable to run or squat. This is precisely the flexion-provoked, activity-limiting pain pattern described in this criterion.

Criterion B — "Unresponsive to conservative therapy for at least 3 months or clinical documentation that conservative therapy is contraindicated (e.g., history of falls due to mechanical instability of hip joint)"

I completed 14 weeks (2026-04-09 to 2026-07-16) of supervised physical therapy — 20 visits — focused on core and hip stabilization with activity modification, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. This exceeds the 3-month conservative-therapy threshold. In addition, I used NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-21 produced only 2 weeks of partial relief. Taken together, this documents a sustained, multi-modality conservative-treatment trial that has failed to resolve my symptoms.

Criterion C — "Positive impingement sign on clinical examination (i.e., pain elicited with 90 degrees of flexion and internal rotation and adduction of the femur)"

My exam findings include positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain, consistent with this criterion.

Criterion D — imaging and absence of advanced osteoarthritis

The policy's Criterion D requires: "1. Imaging (conventional x-rays, MRI, MRI arthrogram) documents morphology indicative of cam-type or pincer-type FAI (See List of Information Needed for Review); and 2. No evidence of advanced osteoarthritis, defined as Tonnis grade II or III, or joint space of less than 2 mm, except when there is mechanical instability."

My MRI arthrogram of the hip, performed 2026-06-13, documents an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement and an alpha angle of 68 degrees. The policy's own "List of Information Needed for Review" identifies "femoral head-neck offset with an alpha angle greater than 50 degrees" as morphology indicative of cam-type FAI — my alpha angle of 68 degrees exceeds that threshold. The same MRI arthrogram documents preserved joint space and Tonnis grade 0, which affirmatively rules out the advanced-osteoarthritis exclusion (Tonnis II/III or joint space under 2 mm) referenced in this criterion.

Criterion E — "Requested procedures must be consistent with the anatomical abnormalities documented"

The requested procedure, CPT 29914 (arthroscopy, hip, surgical, with femoroplasty for treatment of cam lesion), directly corresponds to the cam-type FAI with elevated alpha angle documented on imaging. The procedure requested matches the pathology found.

Additional relevant facts

I have no active infection and no untreated substance use disorder that would affect surgical candidacy. My BMI is 29 and I am a non-smoker. These factors do not implicate any exclusion in Policy No. 160 as I have been able to review it.

Conclusion and request

Based on the criteria in Regence's own Policy No. 160 and the documentation summarized above — 9 months of activity-limiting flexion-provoked pain, a 14-week/20-visit supervised physical therapy course plus 8 months of NSAIDs and a corticosteroid injection with only transient partial relief, a positive impingement sign on exam, MRI-arthrogram-confirmed cam-type FAI with an alpha angle of 68 degrees, absence of advanced osteoarthritis (Tonnis grade 0, preserved joint space), and a requested procedure (CPT 29914) that matches the documented pathology — I believe my case satisfies Criteria A through E as I understand them from the retrieved policy text. I ask that this determination be reversed and the requested hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914) be authorized.

I have enclosed the following supporting records referenced above: [physical therapy discharge note, 2026-04-09 to 2026-07-16]; [medication/injection records]; [MRI arthrogram report dated 2026-06-13]; [surgeon's clinic note documenting exam findings]; [letter of medical necessity from Dr. Marchetti, if available].

Please confirm receipt of this appeal in writing, and advise me of the timeframe for a decision and of any further appeal rights (including Level Two internal appeal and external/independent review) if this appeal is not resolved in my favor. If any portion of this determination was based on policy language not quoted above, please send me the full text of the criteria actually applied so that I may respond to it directly.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Jordan Brooks
[Signature]

Note on sourcing: All text in quotation marks above is quoted verbatim from the Regence Medical Policy Manual, Surgery, Policy No. 160, "Femoroacetabular Impingement Surgery" (https://blue.regence.com/trgmedpol/surgery/sur160.pdf), and from Regence's published Washington member appeal form (Form 4581WA) for the mailing/fax/email routing information, both of which were directly retrieved. No other plan language has been quoted or paraphrased as if it were the plan's own wording. The mapping of the clinical facts to each criterion above reflects my own argument, not additional plan text.
